sources.schedule_rationale: One file per JST day holds that day's hourly points. Past day files stay up for a few days (checked from a GitHub runner on 2026-10-06: the three previous days complete, a week-old day 404). Reading only today's file lost each evening the last run of the day landed before 23:00 JST (18 of 24 hours on 2026-09-28 to 10-02), because scheduled runs start hours late; re-reading three days removes that dependence, and four runs a day leave a missed run or two harmless.

sources.schedule_rationale: The API publishes one value per day via its own lastUpdate field. Its 30-point series cannot be dated -- the per-series dt is a generator cursor that decrements one hour per series in listing order -- so no history is retrievable and a missed day is unrecoverable. Captured twice daily with a wide separation so one failed run does not cost a day.

sources.overlap_strategy: Two endpoints per station: past (7d hourly, 貯水位/流入量/全放流量 only) and current (~50h hourly, adds 貯水量 and percentages). Merged on (obs_fcd, observed_at), current filling storage over the past window's tail. Consecutive runs overlap by 6 days for the core variables and ~26h for storage. By normalised name it overlaps the MLIT/OpenGov delivery (126/127) and the seven per-prefecture feeds (199/209) — de-duplicate at the delivery layer; ~596 stations (583 distinct names) are new. Note 坂本ダム and other repeated Japanese dam names occur at several sites, so de-duplication must key on obs_fcd plus prefecture, never on name alone.
sources.schedule_rationale: The 7-day past window makes the three core variables robust to six consecutive failures; the ~50h current window makes storage tolerate one. Daily is the cadence the shorter window dictates. Schedule paused 2026-09-16; see licence_gate.

sources.overlap_strategy: Append-only accumulator keyed on (prefecture, dam_jp, observed_at); a repeated observation time is written once. The accumulated file IS the series because the source publishes no history.
sources.schedule_rationale: No backfill path exists: historical queries return zero dam rows and the Wayback Machine holds no snapshot of this servlet, so anything a run misses is lost permanently. The source advances every 10-30 minutes, which is a continuous signal rather than a discrete expiring publication; the intended product is therefore an HOURLY sampled series. Running every 30 minutes gives each hourly slot two capture opportunities, so a single failed or delayed run does not create a hole. A twice-daily cadence would capture 2 of roughly 48 daily observations and is not appropriate here. Measured 2026-09-17..24: GitHub delivered 43 of 336 scheduled runs (about six a day), leaving 5-8 observed hours per prefecture per day; a complete hourly series needs the external dispatch trigger described in README.md (Scheduled runs).

sources.overlap_strategy: Every run re-requests every page from Argentina today minus 40 days to today. Pages are stored once per content hash computed after removing the CDN's per-response <script id="f5_cspm"> token, and the CSVs are rebuilt from raw pages keyed on (page_date, box_name, content hash), so reruns and overlapping captures add nothing; a genuine change to a page's data is kept as a new version.
sources.schedule_rationale: 09:15 and 20:15 America/Argentina/Buenos_Aires. Because each run re-reads the whole window, every page gets about 60 capture opportunities; two runs a day leave a 13-hour maximum gap and survive GitHub cron delays or a failed run with weeks of margin. Declared cadence is 24h (one page per Argentina day). Registered and deployed 2026-09-28.

sources.overlap_strategy: Every run reads the whole year-to-date chart of the four reservoirs (Cachi, Arenal, Pirris, Reventazon). A page is stored once per hash of its parsed daily chart data - the time banner, JSF ViewState and timestamped chart ids change on every request and are ignored - and the hourly table of each run is appended to raw/hourly_readings.jsonl keyed on its reading time. The CSVs are rebuilt from all stored pages keyed on (reservoir, observation_date); the latest capture wins and changed values are listed in the revisions CSV, so reruns and overlapping captures add nothing.
sources.schedule_rationale: 07:20, 15:20 and 23:20 America/Costa_Rica (UTC-6, no DST). The chart shows only the current year (1 January to today, later days null) and nothing on the page selects an earlier year, so each value stays visible until the chart moves to the next year. The shortest-lived value is 31 December - published by about 01:00 local (checked 2026-10-01) and gone at the year change - which these runs capture three times; retention_window_hours states that worst case. Declared cadence 24h (one value per reservoir and day). Registered and deployed 2026-10-01. The Internet Archive's 33 captures of the page (2020-09 to 2026-06) can be imported with IMPORT_DIR to restore earlier years.

sources.schedule_rationale: 02:40, 08:40, 14:40 and 20:40 America/Jamaica (UTC-5, no DST). The page shows only the latest reading and replaces it with the next one. The Internet Archive's 30 distinct captures of the page (2021-08-27 to 2026-07-11) can be imported with IMPORT_DIR.
